chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man from whom I buy goods on the condition that there is no defect upon me. Is this valid? And how is it valid? And what is the limit of that? He said, 'It is not proper (valid).'

key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي: is not proper / is not suitable

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying goods with a condition of no defects in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) addresses the validity of a conditional sale where the buyer excludes all liability for defects, ruling that such a stipulation is 'not proper' (la yanbaghi). This reflects the Shia juristic principle that while the core transaction may be valid, excluding all guarantees undermines the mutual trust and transparency required in commercial exchanges, distinguishing between a valid sale and a sound contractual condition.
